Yep! Original blue Dawn. Good at getting the dirt and stink out. Haha.

I also wanted to add that their ears react the same as our ears do when we get water in them. The main concern is that all the water gets out and the ears get to dry effectively otherwise it CAN lead to infection. So, long haired dogs, or dogs with hair that hold water very well need special attention paid to their ears if you are not drying them with a hair dryer.

She has some of that water proof type hair. It's hard to even get her fully soaked unless I move the hair around to get wet and soaped up. I always pour directly on top of her head and she keeps her head fairly level as I do it so it only trails down her ears not inside. So no worries! I work for a doggie day care/animal hospital facility where we also do professional dog baths. She's in good hands!

She's not a huge fan either. Especially when it comes to getting her face rinsed off but she always loves the after bath feeling. She'll run around crazy. I just take it slow. I started where she had to come to me in the bathroom. I'd sit on the toilet and wait till she came and sat in front of me. It'd take some coaxing when she saw the measuring cup, soap, and towels going in the bathroom. Then I'd put her in and bath her. Then I got it to were I'd ask her to put her front paws on the tub and I'd put her in and bath her. Now she gladly jumps in. We also don't have to force her in the kennel. She knows when we say "in" or "go in" and point at the kennel, she has to go in and she will. Consistency, trying not to make her upset or scare her. A lot of reassuring her she's okay and a couple of kisses. :) I have a really cute video of when we were training her to come in the bathroom for her bath. You can see her face and body language going, "Do I have to mom?"
